headline: Rick Wurster, chief executive of the brokerage Charles Schwab, said AI agents should trade for a customer only under rules the customer sets, calling it risky to hand over the keys.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a named brokerage chief gives a clear view on AI trading agents, but it is one executive's opinion.
importance_line: Customers using or considering AI trading tools on platforms such as Robinhood and Coinbase hear a large broker's view on safe use, but it is one executive's opinion and not a rule, and Schwab is not offering a trading agent itself.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Rick Wurster, chief executive of the brokerage Charles Schwab, said an AI agent should trade on a customer's behalf only if the customer gives it "the rules of the road" and stays in charge, calling the idea of "just handing the keys over" "a leap too far" and "risky". Schwab, which reported record third-quarter revenue of $7.17 billion, will soon launch Charley, an AI assistant that can handle administrative tasks such as changing an address but will not be a trading bot.
notes: Yahoo Finance's own interview. The interview day is not stated; the article is dated 16 Oct 2026.
